n1: Ahmes is a robot classmate who's sure he's great at maths. A child has to teach him.
n2: Her words become his code on Vultr. One model writes it, a throwaway gVisor box runs it, and plain arithmetic checks it.
n3: Twenty-four out of forty. A quiz on new problems shows exactly what she didn't say.
c3: Keep doubling both bottoms until they're the same.
n4: This rule never ends. At three seconds the sandbox kills it and deletes the box. Ahmes keeps his last working rule.
n5: Each turn is a few calls to open models on Vultr Serverless Inference, and one throwaway container, listed here with timings.
n6: Now try to break him. Out of memory: killed at sixty-four megabytes. The internet: unreachable. Every box leaves a receipt.
n7: When she's stuck, Thoth steps in: a second open model on Vultr that checks the code against her words, and hints without giving the answer.
thoth: Look at the hundredths place: does 6 or 4 come next? Which number line spot matches that?
n8: An answer isn't a rule, so Ahmes asks for one.
c4: If the tenths are the same, check the next place, and if every place is the same, they're equal.
n9: Forty out of forty, on brand-new problems.
n10: Six lessons from the Year 5 and 6 curriculum for England, each starting from a real childhood mistake.
n11: For parents and teachers, a report of the rule she actually explained, in her own words.
n12: Teach Ahmes. Built on Vultr for Agent Rush.
n_arch: Four open models on Vultr Serverless Inference, and one Vultr server, where every task gets its own gVisor box, destroyed afterwards.
